The verifier: 
x0 = frontiers(I): rows/cols that are uniform... returns set of frontiers (each frontier a frozenset of (value, index)). Actually frontiers gives all rows and columns that are single-colored, as sets of cells with color. For grid I, the gray lines rows/cols.

Wait I is the input grid. It finds frontiers - complete rows/cols of same color.

x1 = merge(x0) - union of all frontier cells.
x2 = leastcolor(x1) - least common color among those. That's... among gray line cells, all are 5, so leastcolor = 5. Hmm.

x3 = shape(I). x4 = canvas(x2, x3) = grid full of 5.
x5 = hconcat(I, x4): concatenate input with full-5 grid horizontally. So x5 has width 2*w.

x6 = objects(x5, F, F, T): objects with univalued=False, diagonal=False, without_bg=True. bg = mostcolor(x5). Most common color in x5? x5 is I plus full 5 grid. The most common color is 5 (the entire right half). So bg=5. Objects are connected components of non-5 cells. So each 3x3 square's non-gray cells (the 8 zeros + center color) form... wait they're connected? The 3x3 square region minus gray lines: within the square, cells including zeros around center. All non-5 cells in a 3x3 block are connected. So each block forms one object containing the center color and surrounding zeros.

So mapping is center color + 5!

Center 3 -> 8. Center 4 -> 9. Center 1 -> 6. Center 2 -> 7. Center 0 -> 5.

So Blue(1)->6 (magenta/purple), Red(2)->7 (orange), Green(3)->8, Yellow(4)->9. Yes matches descriptions.

x12 = fork(recolor, x11, toindices): recolor the object with new color. x13 = mapply over all objects. x14 = paint(I, x13).

So each 3x3 block replaced with center+5 color including the zero cells, gray lines stay 5.

Note: also the block's zero cells get replaced. Gray lines remain 5. And the right appended canvas isn't part of output since paint(I,...) uses original I dimensions.
